newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Man, boy killed in attack on wedding in Karachi.
newsitem.headline: Man, boy killed in attack on wedding in Karachi.

text.p: Two gunmen fired on a wedding ceremony in Pakistan's southern port city of Karachi, killing two people, one of them an eight-year-old boy, police said on Sunday.
They said two young men entered a marriage hall on Saturday night armed with a pistol and an automatic rifle and sprayed bullets at a stage where the bridegroom and his relatives were sitting.
Bullets hit six people. Eight-year-old Mohammad Sajawal and the groom's brother Mazhar Iqbal, 30, died of their wounds and four others were injured.
No one claimed responsibility for the attack and police said they had no word on its motive.
Earlier on Saturday, gunmen killed the head of Karachi's power utility, along with his driver and guard.
Shahid Hamid, 46, managing director of the state-owned Karachi Electric Supply Corporation (KESC), had served as Sindh provincial home secretary from March 1995 to February 1996.
That period coincided with a crackdown against militants of Karachi's ethnic Mohajir National Movement.
A KESC spokesman said on Saturday that many different groups had been "after Hamid", but refused to elaborate.
More than 150 people have been killed in political violence in Karachi in the past four months, compared to more than 500 in the whole of 1995 and more than 2,000 in 1996.
